question: How many commodity vessels will transit the Strait of Hormuz on October 1, 2026, according to Reuters?

calls.reasoning: Reference class is the Reuters/Kpler daily 'Shipping traffic via Strait of Hormuz' single-day count during the post-June-2026 collapse regime: prints of 9, 6, 7, 7, 4, 6, 4 across Sep 7-17 (median ~6), with the Sep 19-20 weekend at 17 for two days (~8/day) after 35-37 the prior weekend. PortWatch corroborates the scale (6 on Sep 6, 8 on Sep 13 vs an 85/day baseline). The last week trends to the low end, so I shade the median to 5. Upside: Oman-mediated Muscat talks announced Sep 18 could restore some confidence, but the April 2026 ceasefire precedent shows traffic did not rebound materially even when fighting paused, so a large jump by Oct 1 is a small-probability branch; the right tail stays fat because the strait ran ~18/day as recently as Sep 12-13. Downside: a renewed tanker-for-tanker exchange or a mining incident could push a single day to 0-2. Polymarket's PortWatch 7-day-MA market for Sep 30 (0-5 at 57c, 5-10 at 43c, >=10 under 2c, ~$45k volume) is a near-miss contract - different source, different metric, different date - but is consistent with a mid-single-digit center; I did not find any market pricing the Reuters single-day figure. Escape above 50 requires near-normalization within 8 days (a signed corridor deal plus immediate convoy restart): priced at 2%.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the Reuters daily 'Shipping traffic via Strait of Hormuz' dispatch (Kpler AIS ship-tracking, published ~0200 GMT the following morning) single-day count for Oct 1, 2026 - NOT off a 10-day average, NOT off a weekend aggregate, and only off IMF PortWatch daily transit calls if Reuters publishes no attributable single-day figure. Dark/transponder-off vessels are excluded by construction.

EVENT WINDOW: one calendar day, Oct 1 2026 00:00-24:00, per the criteria; as of Now (2026-09-21T23:24Z) 0% elapsed, the day begins in ~8.0 days and scheduled resolution is 2026-10-02T12:00Z (i.e. the dispatch published ~0200 GMT Oct 2 is the expected source; Reuters revisions for that same date also count).

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the post-June-2026 collapse regime continues - Reuters prints a mid-single-digit count with the same boilerplate that figures may understate flow because transponders are switched off.

EVIDENCE (source, date):
- Reuters/Kpler daily prints: Mon Sep 7 = 9; Tue Sep 8 = 6 with 10-day avg ~12 (Al-Monitor/Reuters, Sep 9); Wed Sep 9 = 7, 10-day avg ~14 (RFE/RL wire, Sep 10); Mon Sep 14 = 7; Tue Sep 15 = 4 vs 10-day avg ~18, no VLCCs or LNG carriers that day (RFE/RL wire, Sep 16); Wed Sep 16 = 6; Thu Sep 17 = 4 vs 10-day avg ~16, comprising two Panamax tankers, a Supramax and a Kamsarmax (Asharq Al-Awsat/Reuters, Sep 18).
- Weekend Sep 19-20: first Reuters version reported 12 commodity vessels for the two days (Sat: 5 out + 1 empty VLGC in; Sun: 4 out + 2 small tankers in); a later same-cycle version reported 17 for the two days (Sat: 8 out incl. a supertanker + a VLGC and a VLCC in; Sun: 5 out + 2 in). Same dispatch cycle, revised upward - preliminary counts get revised (Reuters via AOL/Yahoo/Tribune India, Sep 21).
- Prior weekend Sep 12-13 was reported at 35-37 vessels for the two days (same dispatch, Sep 21), so the two-day weekend figure fell roughly by half week-on-week.
- IMF PortWatch daily transit calls: 6 on Sep 6; 8 on Sep 13 (its most recent published day as of Sep 21 - PortWatch runs a multi-day lag). Pre-crisis PortWatch baseline ~85/day; Reuters cites ~125 large commercial vessels/day pre-Feb-28-2026.
- Crude flow context: 22 tankers, mostly VLCCs, carrying 42m bbl exited Hormuz in the week of Sep 13; Saudi Arabia and Iraq 43% each. Saudi crude through the strait averaged 2.9m bpd over the prior 6 days vs 700k bpd in August, after Houthi attacks on the East-West pipeline pushed volumes back through Hormuz (Reuters, Sep 21).
- Security backdrop: US 'tanker-for-tanker' retaliation policy approved by Trump; US struck three Iranian tankers Sep 2 after Iranian attacks on shipping, including the fatal attack on the Saudi-owned Sidr (Axios/Al Jazeera, Sep 2-6). GPS jamming and uncleared-hazard war-risk premiums persist; US Navy reported clearing 100+ suspected mines in the Traffic Separation Scheme by Aug 25.
- Diplomacy: Oman's MFA announced Sep 18 that Araghchi and Witkoff, mediated by Badr Albusaidi in Rome, agreed to a further round in Muscat 'in the next few days'. Iran was reported to have rejected US talks Sep 15 and Oman-Iran corridor talks were postponed Sep 16. Open issues in the corridor track: who controls the strait and whether Iran may levy transit fees. No concluded agreement found as of Sep 21.
- Precedent for the recovery path: after the earlier two-week ceasefire (April 2026), wire coverage reported maritime traffic through Hormuz 'remains restricted despite' the pause - i.e. a pause in fighting did not by itself restore transits quickly.

BASE RATES:
- Over all Reuters daily single-day prints found for Sept 2026 (n=7 weekdays: 9,6,7,7,4,6,4): median 6, mean ~6.1, min 4, max 9.
- Over just the most recent week of those prints (Sep 14-17): 4-7.
- Over PortWatch daily transit calls published for Sept 2026 (n=2: Sep 6, Sep 13): 6 and 8.
- Conditional on a weekend day rather than a weekday, the only decomposable data point (Sep 19-20) implies per-day values in the high single digits after revision; Oct 1, 2026 is a Thursday.
- Reuters' own quoted 10-day averages during this period (12, 14, 16, 18) run well above its single-day prints, which is the ratio to keep in mind when translating any averaged figure into a single-day one.

MARKET-INSTRUMENT NOTE (no price given here): human markets exist on Polymarket but none price this exact contract. The live ones resolve off the IMF PortWatch 7-day moving average of transit calls for a specified date, and a separate closed series resolved off weekly ship counts for Sep 14-20 - different source, different aggregation window, different date from this question.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: a machine-readable PortWatch daily series for Sep 14-21 (the public chokepoint6 page returned no data on fetch); any Reuters dispatch covering Mon Sep 21 (the cycle publishes ~0200 GMT Sep 22, after Now); any concluded outcome from the Muscat round; any market whose contract matches the Reuters single-day Oct 1 figure; any published Kpler statement on how far preliminary counts are typically revised.
calls.reference_class: Reuters/Kpler daily single-day commodity-vessel transit counts for the Strait of Hormuz during the post-collapse regime (Sept 2026), weekdays
